summary: The third failed result disproved three task-authoring assumptions: existing Story 18.1 issuer/function behavior could supply an honest RED for the new October adapter, an early context-only migration would necessarily grow with later persisted entities, and an external two-host RED could precede explicit owned-resource authorization. The changed approach makes the missing October production verifier/binding the RED seam, assigns migration updates where setup and approval entities are added, and separates controlled host-composition RED from later authorized PostgreSQL/certificate qualification. The next check is retained-author task self-review, deterministic plan/task validation and a fresh complete-definition review against the unchanged accepted spec and plan.
failed_obligations: Route behavioral RED to the new Story 18.4 production verifier and binding rather than already-correct Story 18.1 behavior.
Assign complete October schema and migration-history ownership after all persisted entities are defined.
Keep external PostgreSQL, Identity and certificate execution behind explicit root-established owned-resource authorization.
affected_assumptions: A controlled verifier around the existing issuer/functions would necessarily fail before the October production adapter existed.
The initial October migration task implicitly covered entities introduced by later production tasks.
A process-level two-host RED could run before the task that establishes its external-resource prerequisite.
changed_approach: Correct only tasks.md: target the missing October verifier/binding through controlled dependencies, attach migration updates and fresh-schema proof to the entity-owning production tasks, and keep controlled host RED distinct from explicitly authorized external qualification.
next_check: Fresh tasks self-review, deterministic implementation-design validation, then repeat independent complete-definition review with the same reviewer.
